summary.intent: Improve an unsatisfactory checkpoint by making the map visualization prettier and adding a workout/activity chart with recent workout data beneath it, then commit a proper checkpoint.
summary.outcome: Added a weekly workload domain module, extended the snapshot schema and write path, added start/end route terminals to the basemap, built a 'form guide' chart and map plate styling in render.ts, wrote and fixed unit/integration tests (426 passing, coverage above gate), visually verified light and dark renders via headless Chrome screenshots (catching and fixing a label collision bug), updated decision docs, and committed the feature.

repo: Design system is a 'newsprint/matchday programme' aesthetic using --stock/--ink/--ink-accent CSS tokens with Georgia serif + uppercase letterspaced sans.
The project follows a graph-first workflow (dataviz skill, graph search) before implementing chart/render features.
Snapshot schema previously had no activity/workout time series — had to be added from scratch (types.ts, refresh.ts write path).
Repo maintains a spec decision log (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-tedlasso-strava-design.md) and CLAUDE.md that should be updated when making design decisions.
Repo has a standing rule against em dashes in code/comments, which the assistant violated inadvertently and had to strip out.
Test fixtures/snapshots can predate new optional fields (e.g. basemap terminals), so new fields must be made optional for backward compatibility.

code.finding: Basemap module needed start/end route endpoints added as optional fields so older snapshots without them remain valid; used to show route direction on the map.
Tuning constants file holds config values like WORKLOAD_WEEKS controlling how many weeks of workout data are bucketed.

Render layer builds both map plate furniture and the new form-guide chart; SVG rects needed a distinguishing class (form-bar) so test assertions could target actual bar elements instead of matching all rects (including a white-out background rect).

workflow: Establishing a green baseline test run before making changes helps confirm which failures are caused by new work.
Searching for existing 'strict shape assertion' tests before extending schemas helps avoid breaking exact-match tests unintentionally.
Rendering an actual preview via esbuild bundling + headless Chrome screenshots (both light and dark themes) surfaced a real visual bug (label collision) that pure unit tests would have missed.
Headless Chrome can reuse an existing instance/profile causing identical screenshots across theme variants — isolating Chrome profiles per screenshot run fixes this.
After a visual fix, add a regression test (not just fix and move on) to pin the corrected behavior in the test suite.

friction: First screenshot attempt produced identical light/dark images because headless Chrome reused its instance; had to retry with isolated Chrome profiles.
Lingering headless Chrome processes needed to be manually killed after screenshotting.
Two test assertions initially collided with unrelated content (inlined CSS containing 'Form guide' text, aria-label containing 'usual'), producing false failures.
An aria-hidden attribute assertion was written backwards relative to actual markup order and had to be corrected.
A test assertion counting rects broke when a white-out background rect was added, requiring bars to be given a distinguishing CSS class.
Four em dashes slipped into new comments and had to be found and removed per the repo's standing style rule.
